messages:
pagerduty-bot: 🔔 INCIDENT ALERT — Critical
pagerduty-bot: Tenant=AcmeCorp | symptom=high-5xx-rate + p95 latency > 5s on /v1/generate | SLA error rate=4.2% (threshold 1%) | region=us-west-2
pagerduty-bot: Paging #eng-oncall. Runbook: https://confluence.redwood/inbox/incidents/runbooks/tenant-sla

eva: On it — thanks. grabbing logs and checking model pools. Is this across all regions or concentrated?

mike: Looks concentrated in us-west-2. I'm seeing a spike of 504s coming from model-serve-3 pool, lots of kv-cache pressure and a few OOMs on gpt-large-quant instances. CPU/GPU memory climbs just before the errors.

arya: Good catch. I'll switch AcmeCorp traffic to fallback model variant (gpt-medium) and add a temporary tenant throttle. Quick commands:

```
# throttle to 5 rps until we stabilise
redwood-cli tenants throttle --tenant acmecorp --rps 5

# route AcmeCorp away from gpt-large-quant to gpt-medium
redwood-cli route update --tenant acmecorp --from-model gpt-large-quant --to-model gpt-medium --weight 1.0
```

arya: Doing that now.

pagerduty-bot: Action recorded: traffic reroute + tenant throttle applied by arya. Suppression rule not applied yet.

luis: I'm seeing that a flurry of tenant health-checks from AcmeCorp are hitting generate endpoints every 3s — those synthetic checks are amplifying load. Suggest we suppress alerts triggered by automated health-check user-agent and add a short cooldown for tenant-level alerts.

eva: Mitigation taking effect — 504s dropped ~7m after the reroute, p95 latency falling to ~700ms. We'll keep monitoring for 30m. Immediate followups:
- Add tenant-specific p95 dashboards
- Change noisy alert thresholds (avoid firing on avg when p95 is the signal)
- Exclude or de-weight automated health-check paths from SLA calc
- Assess customer impact and potential SLA credit window

mike: Created GH ticket #4523: "tenant-alert/AcmeCorp — noisy checks + per-tenant thresholds" and assigned to arya. Link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/issues/4523

arya: I'll work the ticket. Proposed alert adjustments:
- Fire on per-tenant p95 > 3s sustained for 5m (instead of global avg)
- Require min_samples >= 100 for tenant-level alerts
- Exclude path prefix `/health` and requests with user-agent containing `AcmeHealthCheck`
- Add a 10m cooldown after an auto-mitigation action to avoid flapping

sam (acct): Heads up — AcmeCorp is impacted. Early estimate: ~12% of their requests experienced errors in the 00:12-00:48 UTC window. They might request SLA credit. I flagged the account team.

mike: Noted. For post-incident reporting: capture exact SLA window, affected request count, and mitigation timeline. I'll draft the postmortem and include a customer impact section.

luis: Long-term instrumentation action items (I'll own):
- New dashboard: per-tenant p50/p95/p99 latency + 5xx rate, filter by path
- Alert tuning: switch noisy tenant alerts from avg latency -> p95, add min_sample guard
- Dedupe logic: don't page on tenant alerts that are below platform-level impact but above tenant thresholds
Ticket #4524 created for dashboards/alerts.

arya: On-call handoff note: I'm going offline in 30m and handing to mike. Leaving runbook edits in the GH ticket and adding a smoke test for the throttle command in staging.

mike: I'll pick this up. Immediate ops notes added to the incident tracker. Also: we should consider a tenant isolation policy — automatically route tenants to lower-cost model variant if their request pattern trips resource pressure for that pool.

eva: Quick customer-impact summary for the postmortem: 00:12–00:48 UTC, AcmeCorp had elevated errors and latency due to frequent health-checks + model pool memory pressure. Mitigation timeline:
- 00:14 UTC: Pager fired
- 00:18 UTC: Traffic reroute + throttle applied
- 00:25 UTC: 504s dropped to baseline
- 00:45 UTC: Monitoring -> stable

pagerduty-bot: INCIDENT STATUS: Mitigated -> Monitoring. Auto-update pushed to incident tracker.

luis: Action list (owners):
- arya: implement exclusion for health-check user-agent + add cooldown on tenant-alerts (#4523)
- luis: build per-tenant dashboard and switch alert logic to p95 + min_samples (#4524)
- mike: draft postmortem and coordinate SLA assessment with Sam (#4525)
- eva: update runbook with tenant-specific troubleshooting checklist and sample throttle commands

arya: Will add runbook snippets and test in staging tomorrow.

mike: Draft postmortem assigned to me, will share for review in 24h. Scheduling a short retro with infra+oncall+product to discuss tenant isolation and alerting rules.

sam (acct): Thanks team — I'll keep AcmeCorp updated about mitigation and that we're evaluating SLA impact.

eva: On-call handoff to mike in ~25m. Leaving one-liner: if we see similar blast from another tenant, escalate immediately to infra to consider temporary model pool scaling or additional fallback variants.

pagerduty-bot: Incident closed from active -> resolved in monitoring. Reminder: please fill the postmortem template and link PRs to incident tracker.

mike: A few notes for the post-incident change set: prefer p95 alerts for customer-impacting metrics, add tenant-level min_samples, and a dedupe/cooldown to reduce pager fatigue. We'll also add a checkbox in onboarding for large tenants to opt into health-check guidance.

luis: I'll follow up with a draft dashboard tomorrow morning and ping for reviews.

arya: :thumbsup: thanks all — handing off.
